entities.summary: Pope Agapetus I was the bishop of Rome from 13 May 535 to his death on 22 April 536. His father, Gordianus, was a priest in Rome and he may have been related to two popes, Felix III and Gregory I. Agapetus I played a key role in the Eastern Roman Empire's efforts to reassert its dominance over the Western Roman Empire. He met with King Theodoric the Great of the Ostrogoths in Ravenna, Italy, to discuss the status of the Western Roman Empire and the possibility of reunification. Agapetus I's efforts were ultimately unsuccessful, but he laid the groundwork for future attempts to reunify the empire. His papacy was marked by controversy, including a dispute with the patriarch of Constantinople over the use of iconography in the church. Despite this, Agapetus I remains an important figure in the history of the Eastern Roman Empire and the papacy of the Catholic Church.
